newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BK Vision says UBS board should step down.
newsitem.headline: BK Vision says UBS board should step down.

text.p: Investment trust BK Vision, Union Bank of Switzerland's (UBS) largest single shareholder, said developments at UBS in its view confirmed that the bank's management didn't measure up to their leadership requirements and should step down.

BK Vision had been involved in a prolonged battle with UBS aimed at blocking a planned conversion to a single share structure. It had also sought to force the bank to take steps to maximise shareholder values.
"Management of UBS will only find success with the support of a competent management board and convinced shareholders," BK Vision said in a statement.

Earlier on Tuesday, UBS, the nation's largest bank, announced a restructuring of its domestic operations which would result in a special three-billion Swiss franc charge and a group loss of about one-half billion francs for 1996.

The three billion franc charge is being taken to cover the future development of credit risk in its domestic portfolio and the measures will result in a reduction of the group's equity capital, UBS said. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
